ots-before.name: Open Triplestore
ots-before.build: scripts/bench-compare/Dockerfile.ots (fat LTO) with every .rs source touched before cargo build, so the shared target/ cache cannot hand back another checkout's binary; rust:1.94-bookworm

ots-after.name: Open Triplestore
ots-after.image: ots-bench:468-757c2489 (local); its COUNT(*) of the dataset answered in milliseconds (probes/s3/f14.json), which only this branch's code does

client_image: python:3.12-slim@sha256:d764629ce0ddd8c71fd371e9901efb324a95789d2315a47db7e4d27e78f1b0e9 (the local python:3.12-slim; campaign.py pins 78387bc3…, which was not on this machine; the client is the standard-library bench.py under Python 3.12 either way)
commands: docker build -f <Dockerfile.ots with sources touched> -t ots-bench:<tag> .

campaign.py --data-root ~/bench-work/data --cache ~/bench-work/cache --out ~/bench-work/results-468/<run> --ots-image <image> --stores <ots|oxigraph> --scales 1k,10k --workloads explore,features --skip-http-load --poll 20 --max-wait 600 (run from WSL Ubuntu with CLIENT_IMAGE, host_info and swap_used replaced for Linux)
probes/: an interleaved probe (both Open Triplestore builds and Oxigraph running at once, query by query, round by round) from a client container on the same Docker network
order: 2026-10-20: ots-before 1k, 10k; ots-after 1k, 10k; oxigraph 1k, 10k (one machine-lock window, about 45 minutes), after the paired probes of probes/s3. probes/s4 (1k) right after. probes/s1 and s2 are the 2026-10-15 diagnostics, run on the coordinator's ots-bench:462b206c image (built without touching the sources), and are used only for ratios within one run.
note: Concurrency, SHACL and the HTTP load comparison were not run. The machine ran about twice as slowly on 2026-10-20 as on 2026-10-15 (Oxigraph's trivial ASK: 0.56 against 0.20 ms); compare figures within one run only.
